title: Paloma and the Atlas
premise: In the winter of 1919, Ada Ishikawa keeps the Paloma lighthouse on a tidal island whose only link to the mainland is a causeway bridge that closes with the first great storm. When a dying courier washes ashore carrying documents proving that the local magistrate falsified the inheritance records of three drowned fishing families, Ada and her reluctant ally — the magistrate's own estranged son, Tomas — must decide whether loyalty to their community matters more than the silences that have kept it safe. As the armistice negotiations in the capital approach their final signing, the pair smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints manned by men who each owe Ada a different debt. The novel ends at the third checkpoint, where Ada chooses truth over protection: she testifies, the magistrate falls, the families' land returns to the survivors, and she lights the lamp one last time before handing the keeper's post to the girl she saved.
about_author: Edmund Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logbooks along the northern coast. He writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of law and weather.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the final day before the seasonal closure, Ada ferries the last supplies across the causeway and notes who chose to stay on the island — and who was not allowed to leave. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Three Years of Silences
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback woven through present tending of the lamp. She recalls her husband's death and the small lies she has learned to tell to keep neighbors safe. Beat: grief hardened into discipline.

chapters.title: The Storm That Closed the Bridge
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter anchored in Ada's POV. The great storm arrives early; the bridge gates are chained; the island becomes a sealed world. Beat: claustrophobia and strange freedom.

chapters.title: What the Sea Gave Back
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At dawn she finds a half-drowned man on the rocks clutching an oilskin packet. He whispers a name — hers — before collapsing. Beat: shock breaking open the ordered life.

chapters.title: The Courier's Breath
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV introduced. The stranger is Lucan Reyes, a records clerk; Tomas, the magistrate's son visiting against his will, recognizes him from the capital archives. Beat: recognition and fear.

chapters.title: An Oilskin Packet
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. The packet holds certified copies proving the magistrate erased three families' inheritance claims after the drownings. Beat: the weight of paper heavier than iron.

chapters.title: Lucan's Confession
chapters.summary: Lucan's POV, fevered. He explains he stole the documents to deliver them before the armistice signing voids the old courts' jurisdiction. Beat: urgency — a ticking legal clock.

chapters.title: The Debt at Checkpoint One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She realizes the ferry sergeant at the mainland gate once owed her husband his life. Beat: hope entangled with obligation.

chapters.title: Tomas Refuses
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He confronts his father by letter and burns the reply unread; Ada catches him at the fire. Beat: filial loyalty cracking against truth.

chapters.title: The Island Takes Sides
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Rumor spreads; the widow Maren whose family was erased begs Ada to act, while others warn that testimony will bring soldiers back. Beat: community fracturing.

chapters.title: Maren's Land
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A walk through the salt fields her grandfather plowed, now leased to the magistrate's cousin. Beat: inheritance as memory made physical.

chapters.title: Preparing the Smuggle
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, procedural tension. They split the evidence: originals hidden in the lighthouse, copies sewn into Lucan's coat for the crossing. Beat: resolve hardening into plan.

chapters.title: Lucan Worsens
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Fever takes Lucan; a doctor cannot cross. Tomas must choose between waiting and moving a dying man. Beat: compassion versus deadline.

chapters.title: First Ice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The causeway freezes enough to walk but not to trust; she tests every stone herself at night. Beat: solitary courage.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Sergeant's Choice
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The sergeant sees through the disguise instantly — and stamps them through anyway, asking only that Ada never testify he looked away. Beat: complicity as mercy.

chapters.title: What the Sergeant Saw
chapters.summary: Sergeant Brandt's POV, retrospective. His memory of Ada's husband pulling him from a wreck justifies his silence. Beat: debt repaid across decades.

chapters.title: The Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In the mainland town they find the erased families' neighbors prosperous and unwilling to remember. Beat: the banality of convenient forgetting.

chapters.title: A Letter from the Magistrate
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His father's second letter arrives — warm, reasonable, offering Tomas a judgeship if the packet disappears. Beat: temptation dressed as reconciliation.

chapters.title: Lucan Dies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Lucan dies at dawn asking whether the lamp is lit; Ada lights it though no ships need it. Beat: mourning fused with vow.

chapters.title: Burial Without Records
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They bury Lucan outside consecrated ground; Maren's granddaughter, Ilsa, arrives from the island having found the hiding place. Beat: the secret multiplying beyond control.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Sixteen and fearless, she demands to carry the copies to the capital archive herself. Beat: generational impatience meeting earned caution.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The tollkeeper is the magistrate's cousin — the man leasing Maren's fields. Beat: the enemy wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A soldier ransacks their cart while Ada distracts with lighthouse paperwork; the copies pass inside Ilsa's school satchel. Beat: terror in stillness.

chapters.title: Cousin Aldric
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. He suspects everything but lets them pass, calculating that the magistrate's fall might serve him. Beat: corruption hedging its bets.

chapters.title: The Armistice Countdown
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, newspaper fragments and radio rumor. Eleven days until signing; after it, the special courts close forever. Beat: time compressing.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Inn
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A friendly clerk photographs the satchel's contents and sells the images to the magistrate's men. Beat: trust punished.

chapters.title: The Warrant
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Soldiers arrive with a warrant naming Ada as thief of state records; Tomas burns his father's letters and chooses sides aloud. Beat: the break with blood.

chapters.title: Flight Along the Cliffs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A night chase over the cliff path in rising wind; Ilsa sprains an ankle; strangers shelter them in a net-loft. Beat: the coast itself becoming ally.

chapters.title: The Net-Loft Testament
chapters.summary: Fisherwoman Osla's POV. An old woman who lost sons in the drownings hides them and adds her own sworn account to the evidence. Beat: private grief joining public record.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Capital Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The final checkpoint is staffed by a young officer who owes Ada nothing — the cruelest kind of obstacle. Beat: no debts left to spend.

chapters.title: Truth as Currency
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas surrenders himself, confessing to theft of the records, trading his name and career for the officer's hesitation. Beat: sacrifice as argument.

chapters.title: The Officer's Hour
chapters.summary: Young Officer Vey's POV. Alone with the packet, he reads every page and must decide what the uniform means. Beat: conscience under pressure.

chapters.title: Vey Lets Them Pass
chapters.summary: Vey's POV continued. He logs the satchel as 'inspected, cleared,' knowing it ends him. Beat: justice chosen outside the law's safety.

chapters.title: The Archive at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilsa's POV. They file the documents minutes before the armistice terms are ratified, watching the registrar's stamp fall like a verdict. Beat: triumph without celebration.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Fall
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV from custody. His father is arrested at his own dinner table; their eyes meet through the doorway. Beat: pity where hatred should be.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Called to testify despite every promise of silence kept along the way, she speaks the whole truth, naming even those who helped. Beat: loyalty and truth reconciled at last.

chapters.title: Land Returned
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Spring surveyors restore the salt fields; Maren plants the first row herself. Beat: inheritance restored as healing.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Tomas accepts a suspended sentence and exile from the bench; Aldric turns crown's evidence; Brandt retires untroubled. Beat: uneven justice, honestly weighed.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The gates are unchained; the island floods with returning voices; Ada finds she no longer needs her silences. Beat: release.

chapters.title: One Last Lighting
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing. She trains Ilsa in the lamp room, hands over the keeper's log, and walks the causeway at dusk toward a town that finally looks back. Beat: peace earned, story closed.
